narrative.overview:
Earshot is a menu bar app whose face is a particle orb on dark glass. The rest of the interface takes its ground and its colors from the orb: a cool near-black, and a small set of state hues that mean the same thing everywhere (blue for you, violet for working, amber for Earshot's voice). The Activity window always renders dark.

The Activity window is built around one idea: History keeps one day, so the day wraps around the orb as a 24-hour dial. The dial fills the window height on the left; the right side is plain text on the same ground, using system type and system controls.
keyCharacteristics: Cool near-black ground with a faint blue tint.
Dots, thin tracks, and hairline ticks.
System type with one weight step for headlines.
Motion is slow and tied to state.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: A hue has one job. Blue is you, amber is Earshot, violet is working, and orange, red, green are session states. Do not use them as accents.

rules.name: The Amber Is Earshot Rule
rules.body: Amber marks Earshot's own voice and the stretch since you last looked. It does not mark warnings; orange does.

rules.name: The One Weight Step Rule
rules.body: Headlines are semibold, ring names and "now" are medium or semibold at caption size, everything else is regular.

rules.name: The System Type Rule
rules.body: Use the system font and text styles so Dynamic Type settings and macOS defaults apply. The one fixed size is the 24pt recap.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Raise a surface by stepping to the next neutral (Ground to Raised), not by adding a shadow. The callout is the one exception.

dos: Do start from Ground (#0b0d12) and its neutral steps for any new dark surface in the Activity window.
Do take state colors from DialPalette, OrbMode.rgb, and SessionStyle.color, and keep their meanings.
Do use system type styles and system controls; add one semibold step for headlines.
Do keep motion tied to state (orb color change, idle turn, typing in) and honor Reduce Motion.
Do give every dial element a VoiceOver summary or label, since the dial draws its dots in a canvas.
donts: Don't use amber, blue, or violet as general accents or button fills.
Don't add a sidebar of filters or a card around the dial.
Don't use a second type family or weights beyond regular, medium, and semibold.
Don't add drop shadows to surfaces other than the hover callout.
Don't let a ring arc claim work across a gap of more than 30 minutes between lines.
